'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Second Libyan Civil War]], [[Libyan peace process]]
**The [[United States Department of the Treasury]] announces unilateral sanctions on the [[Libyan National Army]]-linked al-Kaniyat [[militia]] and its leader, Mohamed al-Kani, after [[Russia]] blocks the [[United Nations Security Council]] from blacklisting the group for alleged [[human rights in Libya|human rights]] abuses committed in the city of [[Tarhuna]] during the 14-month military offensive led by Field Marshal [[Khalifa Haftar]]. [https://ca.reuters.com/article/idINKBN2852BQ (Reuters)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Texas]]
*****[[Texas]] reports 14,648 new cases in the last 24 hours, a new single-day record since the beginning of the pandemic. [https://dfw.cbslocal.com/2020/11/25/texas-new-daily-record-coronavirus-cases/ (KTVT)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Wyoming]]
*****[[Wyoming]] Governor [[Mark Gordon (politician)|Mark Gordon]] tests positive for COVID-19 and will quarantine for two weeks. [https://trib.com/news/state-and-regional/wyoming-gov-mark-gordon-tests-positive-for-covid-19/article_8e9681c3-12e2-5600-a5bd-4b628306fa23.html (''Casper Star-Tribune'')]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Michigan]]
*****[[Michigan]] announces citations and suspensions on liquor licenses for violating the state's public health order, which was issued on November 15 to control the spread of COVID-19. [https://www.wlns.com/news/health/coronavirus/michigan-businesses-liquor-licenses-suspended-after-violating-the-recent-public-health-order/ (WLNS-TV)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oregon]]
*****[[Governor of Oregon|Oregon Governor]] [[Kate Brown]] announces that the [[Oregon|state]] will relax restrictions on outdoor dining. However, she also said that several restrictions will remain in place until a [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] is available. [https://apnews.com/article/salem-coronavirus-pandemic-oregon-restaurants-e0a786207c07ef2c77670700038911a9 (AP)]
****Officials from the [[First presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]] announces that they have held their first [[Operation Warp Speed]] briefing with [[President-elect of the United States|President-elect]] [[Joe Biden]]. [https://www.politico.com/news/2020/11/25/trump-biden-operation-warp-speed-coronavirus-briefing-440611 (Politico)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ontario]]
*****[[Ontario]] reports 35 new deaths in the past 24 hours, a new single-day record for the second wave of the pandemic and bringing the province's death toll to 3,554. [https://www.cp24.com/news/ontario-reports-35-more-deaths-a-record-high-in-second-wave-of-covid-19-pandemic-and-1-373-new-infections-1.5203720 (CP24)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Saskatchewan]]
*****[[Saskatchewan]] [[Premier of Saskatchewan|Premier]] [[Scott Moe]] announces that the province will restrict capacities of large stores and other public places to reduce the spread of COVID-19. Limits on private gatherings such as weddings and funerals, will also be introduced. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/saskatoon/sask-new-covid-restrictions-moe-shahab-announced-wednesday-1.5815465 (CBC)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bangladesh]]
****[[Minister of Foreign Affairs (Bangladesh)|Foreign Minister]] [[AK Abdul Momen]] and Foreign Secretary [[Masud Bin Momen]] test positive for [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] and will cancel their trip to [[Niamey]], [[Niger]] to attend the 47th [[Organisation of Islamic Cooperation|OIC]] meeting of Foreign Ministers. [https://www.dhakatribune.com/bangladesh/2020/11/25/fm-fs-test-positive-for-covid-19-planned-visit-to-niger-cancelled (''Dhaka Tribune'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****[[Indonesia]] reports a record 5,534 new cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide number of confirmed cases since the beginning of the [[pandemic]] to 511,836. [https://tirto.id/bertambah-5534-kasus-baru-covid-19-hari-ini-pecahkan-rekor-f7oJ (Tirto.id)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iran]]
****The number of daily confirmed cases in [[Iran]] rises by a record 13,843 cases over the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 894,385. [https://english.alarabiya.net/en/coronavirus/2020/11/25/Coronavirus-Iran-records-record-high-of-over-13-500-COVID-19-cases (Al-Arabiya)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****[[Governor of Tokyo|Tokyo Governor]] [[Yuriko Koike]] announces that establishments that serve [[Alcohol (drug)|alcohol]] and [[karaoke]] parlors in the [[Tokyo|capital]] will be asked to close at 10:00 p.m. local time between November 28 and December 17 as part of measures to reduce the spread of COVID-19. The [[Tokyo Metropolitan Government]] will provide [[Japanese yen|¥]]400,000 in financial compensation to each business that complies with the voluntary request. [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2020/11/25/national/tokyo-shorter-store-hours-coronavirus/ (''The Japan Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysia]] reports a single-day record of 2,348 recoveries, bringing the total number of recovered patients to 46,501. [https://www.theedgemarkets.com/article/malaysia-reports-970-new-covid19-cases-while-daily-recoveries-hit-alltime-high-2348-slightly (The Edge Markets MY)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan]]
****[[Pakistan]] reports 3,009 new cases in the past 24 hours, the highest single-day total since July and bringing the total number of confirmed cases to 382,892. [https://nation.com.pk/25-Nov-2020/pakistan-reports-2-954-new-coronavirus-cases-in-one-day (''The Nation'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Croatia]]
****[[Croatia]] reports a new single-day record of 3,603 cases, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 111,617. [https://www.thedubrovniktimes.com/news/croatia/item/10306-coronavirus-croatia-3603-new-cases-of-covid-19-across-croatia-56-more-fatalities (''The Dubrovnik Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
****[[Germany]] reports a record 410 new deaths in the past 24 hours, according to the [[Robert Koch Institute]], bringing the nationwide death toll to 14,771. [https://www.tagesschau.de/inland/rki-meldet-hoechstwert-an-corona-todesfaellen-101.html (''Taggeschau'')]
****[[Chancellor of Germany|Chancellor]] [[Angela Merkel]] announces that the partial [[COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns|lockdown]] will not be lifted until December 20 at the earliest, and may be extended until the beginning of January unless there is an unexpected drop in infections. Additional measures will also be introduced, including requiring masks in schools and limiting private gatherings to five people from two households beginning December 1. [https://www.dw.com/en/coronavirus-germany-announces-tightening-of-restrictions-until-christmas/a-55724968 (DW)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Poland]]
****[[Poland]] reports a record 674 new deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 14,988. [https://polandin.com/50960131/covid19-15362-new-infections-in-poland-active-cases-falling (Poland In)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports a record 507 new deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 37,358. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2020/11/25/russias-coronavirus-deaths-surpass-500-in-new-one-day-record-a72143 (''The Moscow Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey]]
****[[Turkey]] reports 28,351 new cases, including 6,814 symptomatic cases. The country now has 467,730 symptomatic cases. [[Ministry of Health (Turkey)|Health Minister]] [[Fahrettin Koca]] states that for the first time since July, the number of asymptomatic cases will be reported. Turkey also reports a record 168 new deaths, bringing the nationwide death toll to 12,840. [https://www.reuters.com/article/healthNews/idUSKBN2852W3?il=0 (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Uganda]]
***[[Uganda]] reports a record 484 new cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total cases to 18,890. [https://nnn.ng/uganda-reports-record-high-daily-covid-19-cases/ (NNN)]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
***[[Turkey]] purchases 50 million doses of [[CoronaVac]] to be delivered in December, January, and February, said Health Minister Fahrettin Koca. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-turkey-china/turkey-signs-50-mln-dose-covid-19-vaccine-deal-health-minister-says-idUSI7N2HJ00O (Reuters)]
**The number of worldwide confirmed cases surpasses 60 million. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/world/431491/global-covid-19-cases-surpass-60-million-infections-reuters-tally (RNZ)]
*[[Avian influenza]]
**[[Poland]]'s local veterinary authorities states that they will cull 930,000 hens in a farm in western Poland due to an [[Influenza A virus subtype H5N8|H5N8]] [[Influenza A virus|bird flu]] outbreak in the village of [[Wroniawy]] which was discovered yesterday. [https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/poland-to-cull-more-than-900-000-hens-amid-new-bird-flu-outbreak-report-2330256 (NDTV)]
**[[Japan]] detects a new case of what is believed to be a highly pathogenic strain of [[avian influenza]] at a [[Poultry farming|poultry farm]] in [[Fukuoka Prefecture]]. This is the first confirmed case outside of [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. As a result, the prefectural government will cull 93,500 chickens at a farm in [[Munakata, Fukuoka|Munakata]] to prevent the spread of the infection. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/east-asia/japans-bird-flu-outbreak-spreads-to-second-prefecture (''The Straits Times'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on religion]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state)]]
**The [[Supreme Court of the United States|United States Supreme Court]] temporarily blocks restrictions imposed by [[Governor of New York|Governor]] [[Andrew Cuomo]] on religious sites, with [[Amy Coney Barrett]] being the deciding vote. [https://www.newsweek.com/supreme-court-bars-covid-restrictions-religious-services-1550464 (''Newsweek'')]
*[[List of people granted executive clemency in the first presidency of Donald Trump|List of people granted executive clemency by Donald Trump]]
**[[United States President|President]] [[Donald Trump]] announces via [[Twitter]] a [[Presidential pardon|pardon]] of former [[National Security Advisor (United States)|National Security Advisor]] [[Michael Flynn]]. [https://apnews.com/article/donald-trump-pardon-michael-flynn-russia-aeef585b08ba6f2c763c8c37bfd678ed (AP)]
*[[Corruption in Indonesia]]
**[[Corruption Eradication Commission|Indonesian anti-corruption agency]] arrests [[Ministry of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries (Indonesia)|Minister of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries]] [[Edhy Prabowo]] in lobster seed export case. [https://www.thejakartapost.com/news/2020/11/25/kpk-arrests-minister-edhy-prabowo-in-lobster-seed-export-case.html (''The Jakarta Post'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Politics of Lithuania]]
**[[Ingrida Šimonytė]] takes office as the new [[Prime Minister of Lithuania]], becoming the second woman to do so. She also appoints the first gender-balanced [[cabinet of Lithuania|cabinet]] in the country's history. [https://www.lrt.lt/en/news-in-english/19/1284643/lithuanian-president-appoints-simonyte-as-prime-minister (LRT in English)]

'''Sports'''
*[[Belarus at the Olympics]] 
**The [[International Olympic Committee]] announces that they will seek formal punishments for Olympic officials in [[Belarus]] for reports of reprisals against athletes during [[2020 Belarusian protests|protests]] against [[President of Belarus|President]] [[Alexander Lukashenko]]. [https://apnews.com/article/alexander-lukashenko-belarus-elections-olympic-games-europe-1995ce9e1bca0aff75f9b7a70a45ce49 (AP)]
*[[2020 Japan Series]]
**The [[Fukuoka SoftBank Hawks]] sweep the [[Yomiuri Giants]] to win the [[Japan Series]]. [https://apnews.com/article/mlb-baseball-tokyo-coronavirus-pandemic-japan-5df21db93dd436225f3b184aea60fa70 (AP)]
